Indikator 5 measures a specific quality standard across the five administrative regions of Denmark for the reporting period spanning September 1, 2022, to August 31, 2023 [^src1]. The established target for this indicator requires a fulfillment rate of at least 80% [^src1]. However, the data reveals a systemic failure to meet this threshold: neither the national average nor any individual region achieves the standard, with all entities marked as "Nej" (No) for standard fulfillment [^src1]. 

The Capital Region (Hovedstaden) leads the national comparison with a fulfillment rate of 29.4% (95% CI: 26.1-32.9), closely followed by Central Denmark (Midtjylland) at 28.8% [^src1]. At the other end of the spectrum, Southern Denmark (Syddanmark) trails with the lowest fulfillment rate at 20.7%, while Zealand (Sjælland) records a similarly low rate of 22.9% [^src1]. The national average for Denmark as a whole stands at 26.3%, highlighting that even the highest-performing regions fall more than 50 percentage points short of the 80% target [^src1]. 

Because this comparison is built from a single dated table section, broad multi-report trends cannot be definitively established. However, the table provides internal historical context through columns tracking the 2021/22 and 2020/21 periods. Nationally, the fulfillment rate fluctuated slightly, moving from 24.0% in 2020/21 to 22.0% in 2021/22, before rising to the current 26.3% in 2022/23 [^src1]. While Hovedstaden has remained relatively stable—hovering between 26.2% and 29.4% across the three years—Sjælland experienced a notable internal drop from 25.0% in 2020/21 to 16.0% in 2021/22, before recovering to 22.9% in the current period [^src1]. Despite these minor year-over-year fluctuations, no region shows any trajectory that suggests they are close to meeting the 80% standard [^src1].

Summary: Tabellen sammenligner resultater for Indikator 5 på regionalt niveau for 2022/23 samt tidligere år, og viser, at ingen region opfylder standarden på ≥ 80 %, med en national andel på 26,3 % og regional variation fra 20,7 % i Syddanmark til 29,4 % i Hovedstaden.
